sources.cite: AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) reference, S3 Client put_bucket_notification_configuration
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'This action replaces the existing notification configuration with the configuration you include in the request body'; 'You can disable notifications by adding the empty NotificationConfiguration element'; EventBridgeConfiguration '{}' 'Enables delivery of events to Amazon EventBridge'. That EventBridge receives events only for objects created after delivery is turned on, and the event pattern fields (source aws.s3, detail-type Object Created) are from memory of the S3 user guide (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the data engineer at Harbor Lane Foods, a fictional grocer. Partner invoices land in s3://hl-landing/invoices/. Yesterday a change replaced the old invoice Lambda with an EventBridge rule, invoices-to-stepfn, that starts a Step Functions workflow. Since then no invoice has been processed, and finance's close load reads the processed invoices at 09:30.
handover: The same bucket's orders/ prefix still uses an S3 Event Notification that invokes orders-validate (Lambda); that one works.
The bucket is defined in a CloudFormation stack, hl-landing-stack.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the landing bucket, its two kinds of event delivery and what they start.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the rule never fired, how you turned delivery on without breaking anything, and what stops it recurring.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Separates the rule from the bucket's delivery setting.
parts.modelAnswer: The rule was enabled and its pattern was right, but the bucket had no EventBridgeConfiguration, so S3 sent it no events. The change replaced a Lambda notification without turning on EventBridge delivery.

parts.label: How
parts.criteria: Merges instead of replacing; handles the files that landed before.
parts.modelAnswer: PutBucketNotificationConfiguration replaces the whole configuration, so I read the current one, added EventBridgeConfiguration and put the merged document back, keeping the orders/ trigger. The 14 invoices already landed were never evented, so I started them by hand.

parts.label: Lasting
parts.criteria: Puts the setting where the bucket is owned.
parts.modelAnswer: The bucket belongs to a CloudFormation stack; the setting is now in its template, so a later deploy will not remove it.

expertPath.text: Rule enabled and pattern right; bucket has no EventBridgeConfiguration; 14 invoices waiting, 0 executions; TriggeredRules 0.
Merge EventBridge delivery into the current configuration; start the backlog; add it to the template.

scoring.modelReasoning: The rule is enabled and matches the right events, and TriggeredRules is zero, so the events never reach EventBridge: the bucket has no EventBridgeConfiguration. Turning it on is a bucket setting, and the API replaces the whole notification configuration, so read the current configuration, add EventBridge and put back the merged document, keeping the orders/ trigger. Objects that landed before are never evented, so start them by hand. Put the setting in the stack's template so a deploy does not undo it, then check both triggers.
